en.title: Longest Program Suffix Executable in Fixed Time Slots
en.description:
You may only delete some programs from the beginning, keeping a suffix. The suffix runs in its original order, and no program can be interrupted. Each time slot has length k; a program that fits must run in the current slot, otherwise it moves to the next slot. With at most m slots, find the maximum length of an executable suffix.

The standard I/O, examples and editorial were written independently by this site; ranges explicitly marked as this site's are not the source's original constraints.
en.input: The first line contains n m k; the second line contains the program durations. 1≤n,m≤200000; 1≤k≤10^9; the full original constraint is 1≤time[i]≤k.
en.output: Output a single integer, the answer.
en.explanation: The answers are 4, 1 and 5. In the second example you cannot pick a longer range in the middle; the last program must be included.
hints: Binary search the start of the suffix, and count the required slots with the left-to-right procedure fixed by the statement. Deleting a longer prefix never increases the minimum number of slots.
